# Outline — Wren Ashfield route

The route where Caedon's primary love interest is Wren Ashfield, the burned-out
channeler and cloudlane smuggler of the Ashen Circle underground.

## first act

Caedon arrives at the Cog-College and, out of place among licensed talents, gravitates
toward Wren — a scholarship outsider who slips the College's leash as easily as breathing.
He meets the other male students. Wren is guarded; she assumes anyone official-looking will
sell her to the Grey Hands.

Caedon goes to class and sees how ungoverned channeling is punished. Wren hides her
Rust-scarred hands.

Caedon's friend group is sent to investigate ruins as part of a test. Nefarious external
actors intervene — and turn out to be Grey Hand Assayers hunting a fugitive, not students.
Wren's smuggling contacts are the only reason they escape; they emerge victorious but Wren
is now exposed.

Caedon is drawn into the conflict around Wren: the Assayers' hunt for severed channelers
and the Ashen Circle that shelters them.

## second act

Caedon goes training in the woods; Wren teaches him the smugglers' cloudlane craft the
College won't.

Something goes wrong in the world. The school intensifies training, then teleports the
students in pairs to random places. Caedon lands with Wren — in hostile territory where
her kind are shot on sight.

On the run from security services, Wren's underground contacts become their lifeline. They
discover the truth behind the chaos: it is tied to the Assayers' program of mass severing.
Meanwhile another stranded pair is caught, interrogated, and publicly executed.

## third act

Caedon and Wren, with the remaining pairs, seek alliances — Wren opening doors among the
discarded and the smuggler-nets no monarch controls. Caedon exposes corruption at the
highest levels. Some stranded pairs assassinate the rulers of the nations they landed in;
others build lines of communication back to Caedon.

# Route: The Undivided (Dark Polygamy Arc)

A subversion of the harem-game trope. If Caedon never lets himself fall for any single love interest, he falls for all of them — and the shared devotion curdles into something monstrous. This route diverges from the four romance paths at the moment a stranded pair dies, and it does not end in a wedding but in a ruined world.

## first act

Caedon arrives at the academy and meets his fellow students and teachers. He is drawn to Wren, Isolde, Seraphine, and Ember alike, but commits to none — treating each closeness as strategy rather than surrender. He gravitates toward the whole friend group and the other male students.

Caedon goes to class, quietly cataloguing everyone's strengths: Wren's ungoverned smuggler's craft, Isolde's cold Sela precision, Seraphine's Loomwright subtlety, Ember's reckless Vash current.

The friend group teams up to investigate the ruins as part of a test. Nefarious external actors intervene; Caedon coordinates all four love interests together and they emerge victorious. He begins to see the four of them not as choices but as instruments that work best in concert.

Caedon is drawn into the conflicts surrounding all four at once, refusing to choose a side or a heart.

## second act

Caedon goes training in the woods, sharpening himself relentlessly.

Something goes wrong in the world. The school intensifies training, and the students are teleported in pairs to random places. **This is where the route branches from the others:** one of the other stranded pairs is caught, interrogated, and publicly executed — and this time Caedon witnesses or learns the full brutality of it. The death breaks something in him. Having never given his heart to one person, he now vows that he will lose *none* of them, and that the world that killed them will answer for it.
